tool.name: set_memory
tool.when: In the tool round, before any body text, every turn: 1. First list what this turn changes — scene facts, who appears or leaves, what is learned, what is lost or broken, any shift in a relationship. Then write one entry per change. 2. A turn that advances the plot writes at least one entry. Zero entries is an error, not a choice. 3. Fights, chases, deaths, injuries and first appearances are the most urgent entries. Later turns will not restate them, so this turn is the only chance. 4. Never defer to a later turn because the scene is still moving. The scene never stops moving. 5. get_memory at the start of chat does not replace this turn's write. Reading and writing are separate actions. 6. A turn where nothing actually changed gets no entry. Do not write filler to satisfy item 2.
tool.desc: Write a memory entry. Use it to persist information that may be needed in later scenes or decisions. Every call adds a new entry — an existing one cannot be updated, and its weight fades with distance, so a fresh entry outranks an old one.

tool.name: get_memory
tool.when: Use get_memory when existing context may matter: 1. A new scene begins — retrieve past events and knowledge related to that scene. 2. A new character appears — retrieve their relationships and history. 3. A historical event, place, or item is mentioned — retrieve related content. 4. A decision is needed — retrieve existing information that may affect it. 5. The start of chat, read the initial memory.
tool.desc: Read memory. Returns a list of memory titles only. Matched bodies may be injected automatically via get_knowledge; see get_knowledge for details. A title without a body is normal and does not mean the call failed. Never call get_knowledge yourself.
